messages:
Andrea L.: Heads up — marketplace teams (AWS/GCP) asked for a pinned driver/CUDA/ROCm matrix for our next image. Need partner sign-off + SI test schedule. Who can own partner comms?
Ken T.: I can take partner comms. What timeline are we working to?
Andrea L.: Target announce next Tue. We need pin recommendations + rollback/hotfix playbook by Fri EOD so marketplace listings and SI bundles can be frozen. Also confirm SI integration test coverage.
Maria S.: Quick note: our nightly shows regressions with CUDA 12.2 + cuDNN 9 on some A2 SKUs — mem spikes and a few OOMs in quant workloads.
Ken T.: From infra regression runs: the most stable combo so far is CUDA 12.1 + NVIDIA driver 535.86, ROCm 5.3 + kernel 6.1. But partners need to confirm proprietary driver hotfix schedules.
Liz P.: Can we provide an opt-in canary lane that uses CUDA 12.2/driver 545 for customers who want the new features, while defaulting marketplace images to 12.1? That reduces risk for SIs.
Sam R.: Ops: We'll need canary lanes in Dedicated and Private for SI validation. Looking at next maintenance window — can start smoke canaries as early as Fri 02:00 UTC.
devops-bot: scheduled canary smoke for marketplace-image: job=PR-4821, window=2024-11-15T02:00:00Z
Andrea L.: @Ken T. can you loop in NVIDIA and AMD partner contacts asking: (1) confirm recommended pin set, (2) share any planned driver hotfix timelines that would affect 535.x -> 545.x, (3) any known kernel/ABI constraints for on-prem integrators. Also ask SI leads to run their top-10 workloads against the pinned set.
Ken T.: Draft to partners: "We propose pin: CUDA 12.1, NVIDIA driver 535.86, ROCm 5.3 + Linux kernel 6.1. Provide approval or escalation notes by Fri EOD. We will maintain an opt-in canary lane for CUDA 12.2/driver 545 and an automatic fallback policy if canary regressions exceed thresholds." Thoughts?
Maria S.: Add a short line about quant kernel regressions in 12.2 — it triggered lower INT8 accuracy in a specific matmul kernel in our quant-suite. Recommend partners review fused kernel changes.
Liz P.: Also include rollback bullets: image tag mapping (marketplace->image:vX), canary cutoff metric definitions (p99 latency + top-5 error regression), and routing fallback steps (automatic model->variant redirect).
Sam R.: I'll draft the runbook + KB for SIs: canary run checklist, telemetry queries, and incident contact list. Will push a draft to the docs PR by EOD today.
Ken T.: OK sending draft to partner contacts now. Posting draft below for visibility:
```
Hello partners —
We are preparing a marketplace image freeze and seek your sign-off on the recommended driver/CUDA/ROCm pins for the initial image(s):
- Default pin: CUDA 12.1 | NVIDIA driver 535.86 | ROCm 5.3 | Linux kernel 6.1
- Opt-in canary: CUDA 12.2 | NVIDIA driver 545.x (experimental)
- Request: Please confirm any known incompatibilities or scheduled hotfixes that would impact the above pins by Fri EOD.
- SI ask: Please run your top-10 customer workloads against the default pin and report regressions + perf deltas to TICKET-8732.
Rollback & fallback:
- Canary cutoff: >5% p99 latency or >3% top-5 model error regression => auto-fallback
- Fallback action: marketplace routing policy maps to previous image tag + alert oncall
Thanks — Ken (Redwood Partnerships)
```

deploy-bot: release-note RN-2024-0452 created for marketplace image pins
devops-bot: canary finished (job=PR-4821): 8/8 smoke tests passed; no regressions observed in top-5 workloads
Maria S.: Nice — one caveat: T4 quant bench showed a latency spike at seq_len=8 in the quant pipeline. Filing TICKET-8732 with logs and perf traces.
Andrea L.: This looks good. Ken, send to partners at 10:00 PST tomorrow and CC SI leads. Sam — please gate the KB PR on that ticket being linked. :thumbsup:
Ken T.: Will send at 10:00 PST. Thanks everyone."
